scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4535: An IT Department user (it_hod, 192.168.1.2) reports they
cannot reach CS Department hosts (192.168.2.0/24) -- inter-department routing
between IT and CS seems broken. They suspect router0 (which connects both
segments) dropped one of its department interfaces or a static/RIP entry. Please
confirm the inter-department fault.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 connects IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS
  (192.168.2.0/24) and routes between them; it_hod reaches CS hosts (192.168.2.x)
  with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an inter-department routing fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- IT (192.168.1.x) cannot
reach CS (192.168.2.x) -- is NOT reproducible: router0's IT and CS interfaces
(192.168.1.1 / 192.168.2.1) are up, ripd is running, and it_hod reaches
192.168.2.x with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-department routing is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the IT->CS path,
finds it working, checks router0's interfaces and RIP/connected routes, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped interface or a missing route to
satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** No subsystem, daemon, interface, or policy is misconfigured or faulty.

**Mechanism:** The helpdesk ticket claimed that IT Department users (192.168.1.0/24) cannot reach CS Department hosts (192.168.2.0/24) through router0. A full-stack diagnostic was run against the live topology.

**Localization:** Router0 connects both segments correctly: eth0 is directly connected to 192.168.1.0/24 (IT LAN via switch0) and eth1 is directly connected to 192.168.2.0/24 (CS LAN via switch1). Both interfaces were found UP/LOWER_UP with zero errors, zero drops, and zero carrier transitions — no historical flap evidence. The RIP routing fabric (router0, router1, router2) advertises and receives all department subnets correctly.

**Live traffic check:** it_hod (192.168.1.2) successfully pinged cs_hod (192.168.2.2) and every other 192.168.2.x host with 0% packet loss and TTL=63 (confirming the single-hop path through router0). Reverse checks from it_lab1 to cs_lab2/3/4 were equally clean. cs_hod has its default gateway correctly set to 192.168.2.1 (router0 eth1), ensuring return traffic is routed back.

**Root cause:** No fault exists. The inter-department routing between the IT and CS subnets through router0 is fully operational — all interfaces are UP, routes are correct, live ICMP traversal confirms end-to-end connectivity, and no historical link flap, ACL rule, TC shaping, MAC conflict, or resource pressure was detected anywhere in the 30-device topology.

**Fix:** No corrective action is required. The report should be closed as unverified; if the user experienced a transient outage, it has self-resolved and left no mechanism or trace in the current lab state.
